product.name: Demo shop
product.description: Browser → gateway → order API → SQLite, with three third-party services. A tiny app that ships with nacholens, so every feature can be tried without a private repository.

components.label:
Browser
vanilla JS
components.detail: Static page from public/. Calls the API with same-origin fetch under /api and redirects the user to the login provider.

components.label:
Gateway
Node http
components.detail: Serves public/ and forwards /api/* to the order API after a per-IP rate limit (120 requests per minute). Adds an x-request-id header.

components.label:
Order API
Node http
components.detail: Handles sign-in, orders and the sales report. Every route except the two auth routes needs a valid session cookie; writes check the Origin header.

parts.label: GET /api/auth/start
parts.detail: Starts sign-in: stores a one-time state and sends the user to the sign-in provider.

parts.label: GET /api/auth/callback
parts.detail: Where the sign-in provider sends the user back: checks the state, exchanges the code, issues a session.

parts.label: sessionOf (cookie → session)
parts.detail: Finds the session from the sid cookie. Without one it ends with 401.

parts.label: GET /api/orders
parts.detail: My orders, returned with their delivery status.

parts.label: POST /api/orders
parts.detail: Creates an order: checks the Origin and the input, then saves it.

parts.label: GET /api/reports/sales
parts.detail: Sales report, admins only. Passes on what the analytics service returns.

parts.label: trackShipping
parts.detail: Asks the carrier for the status of each order. On failure: unknown.

parts.label: db.js
parts.detail: Functions that read and write SQLite through node:sqlite.

parts.label: fetch(EXTERNAL)
parts.detail: Calls the external services (sign-in, carrier, analytics) over HTTP. The address is EXTERNAL_URL.

useCases.title: Sign in with the login provider
useCases.summary: The user is sent to a third-party provider and comes back with a one-time code that the API turns into a session cookie.

steps.label: Start sign-in
steps.narration: The user clicks "Sign in". The browser asks /api/auth/start; the gateway rate-limits the request and forwards it to the order API.

steps.label: Create a one-time state value
steps.narration: The API creates a random state value and builds the provider URL with that state and its own callback address.

steps.label: Remember the state
steps.narration: The state is written to oauth_state so the callback can prove it started here.

steps.label: Redirect to the provider
steps.narration: The API answers 302 with the provider URL. The gateway passes status and headers through unchanged.

steps.label: Pick an account at the provider
steps.narration: The browser talks to the provider directly, outside the gateway. The demo provider approves at once.

steps.label: Come back with the code
steps.narration: The provider sends the browser back to the callback address with the code and the state.

steps.label: Use the state once
steps.narration: The state row is deleted in the same statement that reads it, so a replayed callback finds nothing and gets 400.
